title: Reset cascade lab protocol and next steps
content:
Summary:

This is a working runbook / lab protocol for investigating a recent class of GPU node incidents we’ve been seeing: short ECC bursts or XID events that precipitate a soft GPU reset which then propagates across the NVLink fabric and causes adjacent GPUs to drop contexts or trigger driver-level panics. Behavior observed: intermittent soft resets (nvidia-smi reports GPU reset), dmesg shows Xid entries with codes in the 13-45 range, and sometimes a kernel oops in our nvidia driver leading to systemd restarting the compute-service. These incidents are sporadic, often after low-level firmware updates or small thermal excursions.

Goals:
- Provide a consistent triage checklist for on-call to collect minimal forensics and restore capacity quickly.
- Provide a lab experiment protocol to reproduce or rule out hypotheses (NVLink propagation, power sequencing, firmware/driver mismatch, marginal memory DIMMs).
- List mitigation steps to reduce blast radius in production and candidate permanent fixes to validate.

Severity and paging guidance:
- Sev-1: Multiple nodes in a single rack experiencing cascading resets affecting >10% of cluster GPUs or disrupting customer jobs in critical pods. Pager: on-call SRE + infra lead.
- Sev-2: Single node with repeated GPU resets causing job failures but clear isolation. Pager: on-call SRE.

Immediate on-call checklist (minimal forensics) — run before rebooting where possible:
1) Capture kernel message tail and XID lines:
   - sudo journalctl -k --no-pager -n 500 > /tmp/kern-recent.log
   - dmesg | tail -n 200 > /tmp/dmesg-tail.log
2) Capture nvidia logs and driver state:
   - nvidia-smi -q -d ALL > /tmp/nvidia-smi-full.log
   - nvidia-smi dmon -s u -c 20 (if stable) to collect util/thermals for 20 seconds
   - cat /proc/driver/nvidia/gpus/*/information > /tmp/gpu-info.log || true
3) ECC counters and nvlink status:
   - for g in /sys/class/drm/card*/device/; do echo $g; cat $g/uevent 2>/dev/null; ls $g/nvlink* 2>/dev/null || true; done > /tmp/sysfs-gpu.log
   - nvidia-smi --query-gpu=ecc.errors.uncorrected.volatile,ecc.errors.corrected.volatile --format=csv -i 0,1,2,3
4) Check power and temperature history from rack PDU (request pdu logs) and cluster telemetry (Prometheus/TSDB).
5) Snapshot running containers and PID maps: sudo crictl ps -a; docker ps -a; kubectl describe pod <affected-pod> > /tmp/pod-desc.log
6) If node is unstable, mark node cordoned and drain non-critical pods: kubectl cordon <node>; kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force

Triage quick heuristics (to decide next action):
- If XID errors are repeated and ECC corrected errors spiking => suspect memory/module marginal or thermal transient.
- If XID followed immediately by NVLink link down messages or NVLink fabric errors in dmesg => suspect NVLink propagation path or link training flakiness.
- If kernel oops in nvidia module stack => capture driver version + reproduce on test harness.

Short-term mitigations (production):
- Auto-evict policy: set node auto-evict threshold in cluster autoscaler for nodes with >N resets in last M minutes (suggest N=2, M=10).
- Disable NVLink for the node as emergency mitigation (boot with nvidia NVLINK_DISABLE=1 / kernel param if supported) — caution: reductions in throughput. Document command and rollback.
- Fall back to driver-compatible model variant (force model routing away from affected node via smart routing rules in control plane).

Lab protocol (order matters):
Objective: reproduce reset cascade and isolate whether propagation requires active traffic on NVLink or occurs at link retrain / power event.
Prereqs: 2-4 GPUs connected by NVLink in the same host (test bench), identical driver build(s), ability to toggle NVLink links if supported, access to firmware/BIOS versions.

Steps:
1) Baseline capture: fresh boot, collect nvidia-smi -q -d ALL, dmesg, lspci -vvv, nvlink topology with nvidia-smi topo -m.
2) Controlled stress without NVLink: boot node with NVLink disabled (if supported) and run a synthetic memory-heavy workload (eg: /opt/bench/gpu-mem-stress) targeting ECC usage to see if memory alone triggers resets. Collect ECC counters.
3) Controlled stress with NVLink active but idle: enable NVLink and run the same stress on a single GPU while other GPUs idle. Observe if link errors appear.
4) Cross-GPU traffic test: use NCCL or a small all-reduce microbenchmark to drive traffic across NVLink (set small messages to exercise link training). Ramp from low to high throughput while collecting nvlink error counters and PCIE/NVLink link state.
5) Power sequencing: simulate PDU hiccup by briefly dropping power to auxiliary rails (in lab only, coordinate with hardware team). Observe whether a transient power dip on one GPU causes neighbor resets via NVLink.
6) Driver rollbacks/updates: repro with three driver builds (current, previous stable, and candidate new). Capture ksym offsets if crash.
7) Firmware upgrade path: if pattern points to NVLink training, test different GPU VBIOS/firmware revisions on a single slot to see if link training behavior changes.

Data to collect per experiment (structured):
- kernel logs (journalctl -k)
- nvidia-smi -q outputs pre/post
- sysfs NVLink counters and ECC counters
- lspci -vvv / dmidecode for slot/board topology
- PDU/UPS trace timestamps
- Prometheus metric dumps for GPU temp/power/PCIe errors around incident

Hypothesis matrix (work-in-progress):
- H1: marginal PCB/slot power rail -> causes transient ECC increases -> per-GPU reset -> NVLink fabric propagates context loss. Test: power sequencing.
- H2: driver link retrain bug in specific driver version -> reproduce with driver roll-forward/rollback. Test: driver matrix.
- H3: NVLink microcode/firmware mismatch between neighbor GPUs -> link flaps and propagates resets. Test: firmware matrix + link stress.
- H4: Thermal/ambient driven intermittent ECC -> stress thermal conditions and inspect corrected/uncorrected counters.

Escalation and communications template:
- If node-level kernel oops or repeated resets after triage: page infra-hw and rl (lead). Use subject: "GPU Reset Cascade — node <hostname> — immediate investigation".
- When declaring customer impact: notify customer-success with short blurb, affected clusters/namespaces, mitigation (evicted and re-routed).
- Weekly sync: aggregate incidents into a single postmortem draft and assign to 'investigation owner' for experiments.

Actions and owners (current):
- Iris Chen: consolidate lab results and run driver compatibility matrix. Target due: 2026-12-05.
- Ravi Patel: schedule PDU power sequencing window with hardware lab and co-ordinate safe test. Target due: 2026-11-30.
- Marta Gonzalez: implement temporary auto-evict rule and safe NVLink-disable script for emergency. Target due: 2026-11-29.
- Ethan Liu: add NVLink/ECC counters to alerting runbook and create Grafana panel to visualize spikes. Target due: 2026-12-02.

Open questions / notes for follow-up:
- Are there any clusters with mixed GPU generations where NVLink firmware differences are more common? (inventory query pending).
- What is the safe minimal window for auto-evict before customer job disruption becomes unacceptable?
- Should we require NVLink logging at boot to be part of node-provisioning telemetry?

Playbook snippets (copy-paste friendly):
- Emergency cordon/evict: kubectl cordon <node> && kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
- Quick ECC counters: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,ecc.errors.uncorrected.volatile,ecc.errors.corrected.volatile --format=csv -i 0,1,2,3
- Collect driver info: (uname -a; modinfo nvidia | head -n 40) > /tmp/driver-summary.log

Postmortem template pointers:
- Capture timeline (first alert -> mitigation -> lab repro steps -> RCA hypothesis -> validated fix + rollplan)
- Attach experiment artifacts (driver builds, firmware versions, PDU logs, lab traces) and mark which hypothesis each artifact supports or rejects.

Notes on safety and risk:
- Power sequencing tests are hardware-risky; coordinate with hardware team and run only in reserved lab racks.
- Disabling NVLink reduces throughput and may increase job latency but is preferable to cascading resets in the short term.

Appendix: useful commands and kernel symbols to capture on crash:
- echo 1 > /proc/sys/kernel/sysrq; echo c > /proc/sysrq-trigger (capture crashdump if asked by kernel team)
- ls -la /var/crash; sudo coredumpctl list | tail -n 50
- github link for driver repro harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/tree/main/tools/gpu-repro-harness

This is a draft. Please add lab results as separate attachments and note which experiments failed to reproduce. The goal is to converge on a low-risk mitigation (auto-evict + driver + firmware combination) we can roll to Dedicated racks in a controlled fashion.
